Hi Anna — thanks for the clear questions. Short version: yes on both, and we have a couple of structured options depending on how hands-on you want procurement to be. I attached a one-page proposal that summarizes options. Key points below.

Option A — FY Co-term + 12m base
- 12 month committed baseline aligned to 03/31 fiscal year (pro-rated for initial partial term)
- Pilot top-up processed as a one-off invoice (non-recurring) at list overage rates; can convert to committed capacity with a true-up credit if you choose to convert within 90 days

Option B — 24m with built-in burst buffer
- 24 month term, lower unit price, includes a 10% burst buffer for transient spikes (6-week window)
- Burst beyond buffer billed as overage, credited toward committed increase if you commit within the next billing cycle

Operational notes:
- Auto-renew can be set to opt-in (default off) for Enterprise/Sales deals; termination notice 60 days works for Blueleaf's procurement cadence
- Co-terming: we can align the first invoice/proration so the annual boundary is 03/31 next calendar year
- For Q1 spike, the recommended mechanism is a pro-rata one-off top-up invoice + a conversion path with a conversion credit (explained in attached PDF).

Next steps: 30-minute alignment call with procurement and finance to confirm PO timing and SOW requirements. Are you available Mon-Tue next week?

Attachment: BL-3581-proposal-v1.pdf (one-pager)

Cheers,

Anna / Lauren — adding pricing mechanics and a recommended path from our pricing playbook. Quick summary so procurement has numbers to work with: 

- 12m baseline: $0.045/token equivalent (example rates for gen workloads) — pro-rated for partial term
- 24m baseline: $0.038/token equivalent + 10% burst buffer included (first 6 weeks)
- One-off pro-rata top-up: charged at list overage $0.062/token equivalent, with a conversion credit equal to 50% of top-up invoice if converted to committed seats within 90 days

Suggested guardrails for Blueleaf: 1) Start with Option A co-term 12m baseline + a one-off pro-rata top-up for the pilot; 2) If pilot maintains >25% uplift for 45 days, convert to 24m and apply conversion credit. This minimizes procurement risk and gives your CFO conversion economics.

I've attached the pricing sheet for the example numbers.
